Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The Kiwi players are on the ground. Imam-ul-Haq and Fakhar Zaman are the openers for Pakistan. Tim Southee to bowl the first over...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Pakistan have a tricky target in front to overhaul and will need to bat sensibly against an effective New Zealand bowling attack for this surface. Will they chase it down and take a 1-0 lead in the series? We will find out shortly. Back in a bit for the chase...

Usama Mir (10-0-42-2) comes up for a chat. The debutant says that he is happy with the performance and thanks the Almighty. Tells that it's like a dream come true to dismiss Kane Williamson for his first international wicket. Feels that they will chase down the target easily.

Having opted to bowl first, the onus was on the Pakistan bowlers to step up and make early inroads with the new ball. They did just that as Naseem Shah struck early to dismiss Devon Conway. The hosts kept the pressure on and did not allow the opposition batters to get off the hook. Just when a partnership was brewing, they got rid of Finn Allen and then the debutant Usama Mir accounted for Kane Williamson as his first ODI wicket. Pakistan continued to chip in with wickets at regular intervals and did not allow New Zealand to get away. The pair of Michael Bracewell and Glenn Phillips did trouble them but Naseem Shah struck twice to remove both batters and that allowed Pakistan to restrict New Zealand to a below-par total. Naseem Shah was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 5 for 57 from his 10 overs while Usama Mir chipped in with two wickets in his debut game. Mohammad Wasim and Mohammad Nawaz took a wicket each.

A decent end to the innings and New Zealand end up with a competitive total on the board. Sent into bat first, New Zealand were dealt an early blow, losing Devon Conway in the first over. Kane Williamson joined Finn Allen in the middle and got New Zealand off to a cautious start. Just when Finn was starting to come to terms with the pace and bounce of the wicket, he was dismissed. The Kiwi skipper followed him soon after to put the tourists in a spot of bother. Daryl Mitchell and Tom Latham then got together and steadied the ship with a 56-run stand. Both the set batters were dismissed in the space of five overs which meant New Zealand were struggling at 147-5. Michael Bracewell and Glenn Phillips then resurrected the innings with a 66-run partnership. The dismissal of Glenn meant the visitors lost their way in the innings. However, Mitchell Santner and Tim Southee struck a few lusty blows towards the end to help New Zealand cross the 250-run mark.
Naseem serves another slower one, a low full toss outside off at 102.3 kph, Southee swings and misses. They steal a bye. New Zealand end on 255 for 9.

Slower one again, full and around off at 109.6 kph, Southee tries to heave but is early into the shot. His bottom hand comes off the handle and it flies down to deep mid-wicket. They cross for a couple of runs as the throw from the deep is quite weak.
Very full and on middle, Ferguson hits it across the line to mid-wicket and crosses for a run.
Lockie Ferguson is the last man in for New Zealand.

OUT! CAUGHT! The slower one does the trick and Naseem gets his second ODI fifer. The young pacer does 'Sajda' to thank the Almighty. Fuller in length, around middle and leg at 102.1 kph, Mitchell Santner tries to go hard with his drive but is early with his shot. He ends up slicing it towards extra cover where Mohammad Nawaz makes no mistake.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Nawaz b Naseem Shah

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a length around middle, at 120 kph, Southee drags his attempted heave to deep square leg for a single.
FOUR! 250 up for the Black Caps! Full toss outside off, Southee throws his hands at it and slices it over backward point for a boundary.
Fuller and around middle, Santner forces it down to wide long off and picks up a couple of runs. 10 from the over again!
A bit short and on off, Santner gives himself room to punch through the line but it takes the inside edge and strikes him onto the pads.
FOUR! Up and over! Santner is playing a vital knock. Fuller again from Wasim, around leg, Santner clears his front leg and lifts it cleanly over wide mid off.
Fuller in length, around leg, Southee initially looks to shuffle across but then steps back to push it down to long on. Gets a run.
Fires it in, very full and around leg, Southee clips it towards wide long on and collects two runs.
Fuller and on middle, eased down to mid off for a single.
Mohammad Wasim (7-0-33-1) is back on.
Fuller and on leg at 141.7 kph, Santner flicks early and it goes off the toe end. Falls safely wide of mid on and they cross. 10 from the over!
FOUR! Nice placement! Back of a length on off, angling away, Mitchell Santner gives himself some room and smashes it through point for a boundary.
Full again, on middle, heaved through square leg for one.
Full and on middle, angling in, Tim flicks it aerially, wide of mid on and collects another couple of runs.
Fuller and on off, Southee drives it past the bowler and Wasim chases it down from mid on. He makes a diving stop and prevents a boundary. Only two runs.
Full in length and close to off, shaping away late, Southee pushes inside the line and misses.
Another bumper, around leg, Santner ducks at the last moment.

What a delivery! Haris Rauf follows the batter down the leg side with a short ball, Santner tries his best to deflect late but it goes closely past his gloves to the keeper. Rizwan collects on one bounce.
Bouncer outside off, Santner stays back and offers no shot. He looks at the square leg umpire but gets no signal.
Shortish and around middle, Santner gives himself room and strokes it square of the wicket on the off side. Bags a couple.
Angles in a length ball from around off, Santner defends it from the back foot to short cover.
FOUR! Timing! Back of a length and outside off, Mitchell Santner sits on the back foot and steers it through backward point for a boundary.
Fuller and around off, bending in a bit, Southee takes a step down the track and defends it safely. Naseem smiles and so does Southee. What an over!
Tim Southee is the new man in and he will face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! SOUND OF TIMBER! Naseem Shah bags his fourth wicket and is on a hat-trick. The crowd is jubilant. A terrific inswinging yorker, around off at 143.5 kph and tailing into the batter, Henry Shipley has no idea about it. He tries to dig it out but by the time his bat comes down, the ball has sneaked through and gone on to rattle the stumps.
The debutant Henry Shipley comes out to bat.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! Naseem has his third. He delivers it on a shortish length around off, at 141 kph, Michael Bracewell steps back to smash it through the line but gets a thick inside edge onto the stumps. A big blow to the Black Caps as Bracewell was the set batter and he could have taken them to a score near 270-280.

Just short! Naseem attempts the slower one but it turns out to be a dipping full toss on off, Bracewell hits through the line and it goes aerially towards mid off. Babar puts in a dive but only gets a hand on it. Two runs taken.
Fractionally short and on off, Santner pushes it from the back foot to covers and takes a single. Pakistan won't mind this much!
A 140.4 kph delivery, on a length around off and nipping away, Santner stays back to push inside the line and misses.
Fuller and off, Santner opens the face of his bat and eases it through cover-point for a single.
Shortish and on off, Bracewell mistimes his pull shot down to long on and rotates the strike.
A touch short in length, around off, Santner bends his back knee and guides it through cover-point for a run.
Back of a length, on top of off, Santner plays it down from the back foot to point.
Length delivery on off, Bracewell punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Full and on off, from 'round the wicket, Michael Bracewell drives it to covers.
Mitchell Santner is the next batter in for New Zealand.

OUT! CAUGHT! Naseem gets the wicket of the dangerous batter. Hurls across a length ball around middle, Phillips stays back to heave it on the leg side but it takes the toe end of his bat. The ball towers towards mid off where Babar Azam takes a simple catch. A timely breakthrough for the home team as this partnership had the capacity to power New Zealand at the backend of the innings.
Commentary.Howout: c Babar Azam b Naseem Shah

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off, pushed to covers.

Fuller and outside off, Bracewell walks across to play the paddle scoop but gets an inside edge. It goes behind, on one bounce to the keeper and Rizwan does well to collect it. They steal a quick run. The umpire has given it as a leg bye. Hmm...
Wide called for height! A slower bumper outside off, Michael Bracewell stays back and allows it through.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and bunts it to mid off for a quick run.
Width there outside off, short in length, Bracewell opens the face of his blade and guides it down to third man for a single.
Fuller and on off, Glenn Phillips goes hard at it and slices it over covers for a single.
Drifting down the leg side, perhaps a slower one, Bracewell flicks it in the air and it goes safely to deep square leg. Two runs taken, 14 from the over!
SIX! Gone the distance! Haris Rauf cooks up a short ball around off, Michael Bracewell rides the bounce and hammer-pulls it over deep square leg for a flat maximum.
Full and on middle, at 142.7 kph, Glenn Phillips knocks it down to long on for a single. 200 comes up!
Back of a length on off, Bracewell pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Take that, says Rauf. He hurls across a bouncer, around middle, Michael Bracewell tries his best to pull but misses.
FOUR! Well placed! Haris Rauf delivers it full and outside off, Michael Bracewell leans forward and crunches it past the diving mid off fielder for a boundary. The 50-run stand comes up!
Haris Rauf (5-1-30-0) is back into the attack.
On a length and just outside off, at 142.4 kph, Glenn Phillips stays back and taps it down to point.
Serves it on a length around off, Glenn Phillips plays from the back foot and hits it straight to covers.
Full and outside off, Bracewell tries to drive but it takes the outside edge and runs down to third man. Another run.
FOUR! Lovely use of the bottom hand. Length ball around leg, Michael Bracewell swings it over mid on and the ball races away to the fence.
Beaten! Delivers it on a good length around off, angling away, Michael Bracewell pushes inside the line and misses.
Back of a length on off, Glenn Phillips pushes it from the back foot, past the cover fielder for a single.
Pitches it up and outside off, Phillips strokes it to sweeper cover for a single. 8 from the over!

A little sloppy from Pakistan here. On a length around off, Phillips plays it down to covers for a quick run. Again the fielder misses his shy at the striker's end and the batters collect one overthrow.
Misses out! A low full toss on middle, Glenn pushes it down to mid on.
Fuller and outside off, driven through cover-point for a brace.

Lands it on a length and around off, Glenn taps it down to short cover and crosses for a brisk run. The fielder misses his shy at the striker's end and Rizwan also fails to gather the ball. They get one more as an overthrow.
Fuller and on middle, it's eased down to long on for a single.
Powerplay 3 time. One extra fielder, i.e. 5 can now be put outside the 30-yard circle till the end of this inning.
Good-length on off, straightens after pitching, Glenn Phillips tries to defend and gets it from the outer part of the bat towards backward point for a dot.

SIX! Glenn Phillips finally gets one away! Naseem Shah bowls this one a length but down the leg side, sits up nicely for Glenn Phillips who nonchalantly flicks this one from the crease. Gets plenty of bat on it and clears the deep backward square leg fence for a maximum.
Four dots to start the over! On a length on off by Naseem Shah, Glenn Phillips pushes it to covers for a dot
Naseem Shah persists with a delivery short of a length at the stumps, Glenn Phillips defends this one back to the bowler.
Short of a length around off, Glenn Phillips tries to punch this one on the off side but miscues it to mid-wicket for a dot.
Back of a length and angling into the batter, Glenn Phillips tucks this one straight to mid-wicket for a dot.
Naseem Shah comes back into the attack. 1 for 20 in his 4 overs so far.
FOUR! SHOT! Mohammad Wasim bowls it on a length outside off, Michael Bracewell picks the length early and presents a full face of the bat. Lofts it over the bowler's head and collects a boundary.
Mohammad Wasim nails the yorker on middle, Michael Bracewell squeezes this one out on the off side.

Appeal for run out! Short and outside off by Mohammad Wasim, Glenn Phillips punches this one to the left of backward point and sets off for a quick single. The fielder there collects it cleanly and hits the stumps at the striker's end. The third umpire is referred but the replays show that Michael Bracewell had made it in safely.
Back of a length at the stumps, Glenn Phillips can only work this one to mid-wicket for a dot.
On a length and on leg, Glenn Phillips defends this one down the wicket for a dot.
Fuller and angling in on leg, Glenn Phillips pushes it straight to mid on.
Full delivery outside off, Michael Bracewell gets forward and defends this one from the crease. Usama Mir ends his spell with figures of 2 for 42 in his 10 overs.
Googly, short and at the stumps, Michael Bracewell blocks this one out from the crease.
Fuller outside off by Usama Mir, Michael Bracewell pushes this straight to covers for no run.
Naseem Shah is warming up. New Zealand will be getting a lot of pacers to face in the end overs. That could work in their favour.
Wrong 'un, fuller on leg, Michael Bracewell tries to work it on the leg side but mishits it to extra cover.
Short outside off and turning away from the batter, Glenn Phillips eases this one to covers and takes a single.
Short and turning in on off, Michael Bracewell opens the bat-face and plays it fine on the off side. Imam-ul-Haq at short third man dives to his right and keeps it to one.
Fuller and angling in at the stumps, Glenn Phillips drives this one to the left of the bowler but Mohammad Wasim makes a good half-stop in his followthrough.
On a length around off, Michael Bracewell guides this one from the crease towards deep cover for a single.
Short of a length at the stumps by Mohammad Wasim, Michael Bracewell defends this one with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Good-length delivery, slanting in on middle, Glenn Phillips pushes this one gently towards mid on and takes a quick single.
Back of a length on middle, Glenn Phillips punches this one off the back foot to covers for a dot.
On a length and angling into the pads, Glenn Phillips clips this one nicely off his hips. Hits it in front of deep square leg and collects a brace.
Change in bowling. Mohammad Wasim (4-0-16-1) comes back into the attack.
Full and outside off by Usama Mir, Michael Bracewell drives it straight to cover for a dot.
Beauty! Slower and short on off, Michael Bracewell tries to defend this one but gets beaten by the turn.
Short and outside off, Michael Bracewell punches this one past backward point and comes back for the second.
Slower and fuller outside off, Michael Bracewell defends this one to covers for a dot.
FOUR! Usama Mir bowls a low full toss outside off, Michael Bracewell does not miss and drives it through covers. Times it too well and it goes for a boundary.
Short and turning in on middle, Michael Bracewell tries to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge back onto his pads. The ball falls to the left of Mohammad Rizwan behind the wickets.
Around off, Michael Bracewell closes the face of his bat and works it wide of short fine leg for one. Mohammad Nawaz is done with his 10-over spell, 1 for 38 - a great effort!
Fires a full ball around leg, Bracewell flicks but finds mid-wicket.
Pitches it up and on middle, it's wristed down through mid on for a single.
Loopy delivery on off, Bracewell uses his feet and pushes it to long on for one.
Flatter and on middle, straightening from there, Glenn gets back and plays it at the last moment. Eases it through mid on for a run.
Quicker and shorter on off, Michael Bracewell gets back and knocks it down to long on for one.
Floated full toss around middle, Glenn Phillips only manages to push it back to the bowler. Just one run off the over!
Quicker one, short and outside off, Glenn defends it back from the crease.
Flatter and on off, skidding in, Glenn Phillips goes back and forces it to covers.
Beaten! Superb delivery. Slower through the air, full and around off and turning away, Phillips tries to drive but misses.
Full and on off, pushed to point.

Could have easily dragged it on! Slightly short and on off, Michael Bracewell gets back to play the reverse pull but it takes the inner edge. The ball falls on his pads and deflects past the stumps to short fine legt. They cross.
Too full this time, around off, Bracewell eases it down to long on for a single.
Bowls it full and around off, Michael Bracewell defends it off the front foot.
Quicker one, full and on the pads, it's worked towards short fine leg for a single. 150 comes up!
Flatter and fuller, around off and straightening a bit, Glenn defends it from the back foot.
Fires it full and on middle, Bracewell again hangs back and this time tucks it past mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter and a touch short on off, Michael Bracewell gets back and helps it to short mid-wicket.
Flighted and around off, turning away a bit, Glenn Phillips defends it off the front foot to covers.
Again bowls it outside off but this time the length is short, Michael Bracewell cuts it to deep point and gets off the mark with a single.
Fuller in length and wide outside off, Bracewell leaves it alone.

Time for Drinks! With still 18.3 overs remaining in the innings, New Zealand have lost half their side. The onus is now on Glenn Phillips to resurrect the innings with support from the lower order. On the other hand, Pakistan will be looking to wrap up the innings quickly. Also, Michael Bracewell now joins Glenn Phillips in the middle.

OUT! Latham holes out! New Zealand lose another set batter and will have to rebuild. Usama sends across a short delivery around off, Latham quickly shifts his weight on the back foot and attempts to pull it across the line. But all he manages is a big top edge and the ball flies in front of the square on the leg side. Fakhar Zaman is stationed in the deep and he grabs the skier safely. Every time a partnership has blossomed for the Black Caps, Pakistan have successfully managed to nip it in the bud.
Commentary.Howout: c Fakhar Zaman b Usama Mir

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish around off, Latham moves back and pushes it to mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, cut through cover-point for a run.
Usama Mir (6-0-31-1) returns to the attack. A slip in place for him.
Fuller around off, Latham connects too well with his reverse sweep but fails to find the gap. Plays it straight at short third man.
Flatter and on middle, knocked down to long on for a run.
Flighted and around off, swept to deep square leg for a single.
Walks forward to a full ball and helps it to mid-wicket.
Goes on the back foot and cuts it through point for one.
Goes on the back foot and defends it to short mid-wicket.
Fuller outside off, Tom Latham tries to cut this one on the off side but gets a thick outside edge that goes on the bounce towards short third man.
Fullish delivery on off by Agha Salman, Glenn Phillips knocks this one down to long off for a single.
Short and at the stumps, Glenn Phillips works this one in front of mid-wicket for a dot.
FOUR! Agha Salman misses his radar and bowls this one fuller and down the leg side, Glenn Phillips executes the sweep and helps it past short fine leg for a boundary.
Short and outside off, Glenn Phillips can only push this one back to the bowler.
Full and turning away outside off, Tom Latham gets forward and pushes it to deep cover for a single.
Agha Salman is back on after just one over from Haris Rauf in his third spell.
Quicker and shorter outside off, Glenn Phillips goes back and pushes this delivery to covers for a dot.
Full delivery on off, Tom Latham sweeps this one along the ground towards deep backward square leg for a single.
Fuller around off by Mohammad Nawaz, Tom Latham gets inside and clips it straight to mid-wicket for a dot.
Full delivery on middle, Glenn Phillips drives this one down to long off for a single.
Full and drifting into the batter, Glenn Phillips tries to work it on the leg side but cannot get it away.
Fuller and angling in on middle, Glenn Phillips defends this one with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, Glenn Phillips punches this one off the back foot to deep cover and takes a single.
Short of a length outside off by Haris Rauf, Glenn Phillips lets the ball come to him and steers this one wide of backward point. Opens his account with a brace.
Good-length delivery on off, Tom Latham tries to defend this one but gets an inside edge back onto his pads. The ball rolls towards covers and the batters cross for a single
FOUR! A pacy delivery, full and at the pads, Tom Latham clips this one nicely and times it too well. Gets it to the left of deep square leg for a boundary this time.
Back of a length on middle by Haris Rauf, Tom Latham nudges this off the back foot to the left of deep square leg for a couple of runs.
Short and angling in on off by Haris Rauf, Tom Latham defends this from the crease towards mid off for a dot.
Haris Rauf is back on. 4-1-20-0 are his figures thus far.
Short outside off by Mohammad Nawaz, the ball keeps a bit low but Glenn Phillips goes back in his crease and punches it to extra cover for a dot.
Glenn Phillips walks in next. Slip is in place, Pakistan are attacking.

OUT! TIMBER! Beauty from Nawaz! This is a top delivery by Mohammad Nawaz! Bowls this one slower and a touch fuller on middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell looks to defend this one by getting forward but gets beaten by the turn. The ball spins past the outside edge and crashes into the middle stump. A much-needed breakthrough for Pakistan.
Short and on off, Daryl Mitchell taps this one back to the bowler for a dot.
Fuller on middle by Mohammad Nawaz, Tom Latham reverse-sweeps this one along the ground to deep point for a single.
Full at the stumps, Daryl Mitchell shimmies down the track and works this one to the right of long on. Tom Latham wants the second but has to settle for a single.
Short and on off by Mohammad Nawaz, Daryl Mitchell goes back in his crease and pushes this one back to the bowler.
Short and at the pads, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and nudges it towards square leg for a run.
Fuller around off, Daryl Mitchell flicks this one straight to mid-wicket for a dot.
Short and turning away on off, Tom Latham goes back and pushes this one down to long on for a single.
Fuller outside off by Agha Salman, Tom Latham drives this one straight to covers for a dot.
Fuller on middle, Daryl Mitchell reverse-sweeps this one towards deep point for a single.
Fuller on off, Tom Latham goes for the paddle sweep on the leg side but decides to play it from the back of the bat at the last moment. Hits it to short third man for a single.

Yet another sweep shot to a full ball around off, this time it goes straight to Imam-ul-Haq at deep square leg and they get a single. The 50-run stand comes up, off 64 balls. At the halfway mark, New Zealand are 119 for 3.
Fuller and on off, it's swept firmly to deep square leg and a slight fumble from Imam-ul-Haq makes the second run easy for the batters.
Slower through the air, full and around off, Latham walks forward to flick but misses. He is hit on the front pad.
Flatter and shorter on off, Tom goes back and punches it back to the bowler.
Loopy and full on off, Mitchell eases it off his front foot to long off. Takes a single.
Fuller and around off, Tom uses his feet and knocks it down to long on for a run.
A touch short and on off, skidding in, Tom Latham goes on the back foot and cuts it through point for a single.
Darts a full ball on the pads, Mitchell helps it wide of mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Gets forward and drives it square of the wicket on the off side. Nawaz stops it with a dive and they cross.
Extra loop on this delivery, full and on middle, Daryl Mitchell wrists it through mid-wicket and takes the first run quickly. He wants the second run but Tom is not ready.
Short and outside off, Latham goes back and punches it to deep point for a single.
Loopy and full around middle, Tom tickles it to mid-wicket and sets off for a run. He is sent back.

Angles in a quicker full ball on middle, Mitchell helps it off his pads to short mid-wicket. The Pakistan spinners are bowling disciplined lines and they are assisted by the watchful approach of the current batters.
Leans forward to a full ball around off and defends it back on the surface.
Fetches a full ball from around off and sweeps it through backward square leg for a single.
Tossed up around off, Latham flicks it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Fires it full and around off, Mitchell plays it down with soft hands to cover-point for a quick run.
Flatter arm ball on off, Mitchell punches off the back foot to short mid-wicket.
Change of ends for Mohammad Nawaz.
Flighted delivery outside off, Latham drives again but finds the cover fielder. This stand has moved to 38 runs.
Around off, driven to covers where the fielder fumbled but no run was taken.
Floated around off, full in length, Daryl Mitchell comes up with another sweep shot. This time Haris Rauf makes a diving stop at short third man as the batters cross.
Fuller and outside off, this time it has been driven through the cover region for a run.
Loopy and full, wide outside off, Tom drives but finds the cover fielder.
Full and around off, Daryl plays the reverse sweep towards short thrid man. The fielder makes a diving stop and they cross for a hesitant single.
Agha Salman comes on to bowl, replacing Mohammad Nawaz.
Another quicker one on off, Latham uses the crease and helps it to short mid-wicket.
Shortish and on off, defended on the leg side.

Uppish but safe! Short delivery, around off and staying low as it turns into the batter, Latham checks his shot from the back foot and pushes it aerially towards short mid-wicket. Doesn't carry to the fielder.
Flighted delivery on the pads, it's tucked through square leg for a run.
Flatter and shorter on off, Latham moves back and hits it square of the wicket on the off side for one.
Wide! Quicker one, full and down the leg side, Tom tries to sweep but misses. A good take by Rizwan.
A touch short and on middle, Daryl moves back and works it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Short and on off by Mohammad Nawaz, Tom Latham goes back in his crease and plays this one back to the bowler.
Fuller and angling into the batter, Daryl Mitchell drives this one to the left of mid-wicket and takes a single to bring up the hundred for New Zealand.
Touch fuller on off, Tom Latham goes back and pushes this one down to long on for a run.
Flighted, fuller on off, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and gets to the pitch of the delivery. Knocks it down to long on and takes a single.
Fuller around off by Mohammad Nawaz, Daryl Mitchell defends this one back to the bowler.
Short and turning in on middle, keeps a bit low but Tom Latham still manages to punch it down to long on for a single.
Short and quicker on off, Daryl Mitchell pushes it to backward point and Tom Latham wants a single but gets sent back.
Beaten! Slower and fuller outside off, Daryl Mitchell gets forward to defend but the ball spins past the outside edge.
Good running! Short and outside off by Usama Mir, Daryl Mitchell punches this one past backward point. Hits it to the left of deep cover which allows him to come back for the second.
Fuller outside off, Tom Latham steers this one towards short third man and takes a single.
Floated, fuller outside off by Usama Mir, Daryl Mitchell plays this one with the turn and pushes it to covers for a single.
Short and turning away on off, Daryl Mitchell taps this one off the back foot to mid-wicket for a dot.
Short and at the stumps, Tom Latham pushes this one off the back foot back to the bowler.

FOUR! Nicely played! Mohammad Nawaz bowls this one fuller on leg, and Tom Latham gets into the position early and reverse-paddles this one fine on the off side. Gets it the right of Mohammad Wasim at short third man for a boundary.
Short and on middle, Daryl Mitchell works this one off the back foot towards square leg for a run.
Tossed up, a touch fuller outside off, Daryl Mitchell defends this one from the front foot to cover for no run.
Fuller around off by Mohammad Nawaz, Tom Latham gets inside the line of the delivery and paddle-sweeps this one to fine leg for a run.
Short and angling into the pads, Daryl Mitchell stays in the crease and tucks this one to the left of short fine leg for a single.
Fuller at the stumps, Daryl Mitchell gets forward and drives this one to the left of mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller on leg by Usama Mir, Tom Latham works this one towards short fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Short and punished by Tom Latham! Usama Mir bowls this one short and at the stumps, Tom Latham picks the length early and dispatches this one over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Short and turning in on middle, Tom Latham defends this one off the back foot to mid-wicket for a dot.
Fullish delivery on off, Daryl Mitchell pushes this one down to long on for a single.
Fuller on off by Usama Mir, Tom Latham gets forward and works it to covers for a single.
Flighted, fuller on off, Tom Latham gets down on one knee and sweeps this one uppishly towards deep square leg for a single.
Short and drifting into the batter, Daryl Mitchell pushes this one down to long on for a single.
Fuller around off by Mohammad Nawaz, Tom Latham guides this one fine to short third man for a single.
Fuller and angling on leg, Daryl Mitchell nudges this one towards square leg for a single.
Slower and a touch fuller on off, Daryl Mitchell advances down the track but can only push this one towards mid-wicket for a dot.
Mohammad Nawaz starts with a full-length delivery outside off, Tom Latham paddle sweeps this one down to fine leg for a single.
Mohammad Nawaz comes into the attack.
Perhaps a googly, around leg, Mitchell works it off his pads to short fine leg. End of a successful over for the debutant.
A low full toss around off, Latham paddles it down to fine leg for another run.
Fuller around off, Daryl gets forward and strokes it to deep cover for a run.
Too full and around leg, Latham gets down and sweeps it to fine leg for a single.

Time for Drinks! After being sent into bat, it has been a sedate start by New Zealand. They did lose Devon Conway early but Finn Allen and Kane Williamson kept the scoreboard ticking. However, they have been pegged back slightly by the loss of both set batters. Also, Tom Latham is the next batter in for New Zealand and Pakistan will look to build on the pressure.

OUT! BOWLED! What a wicket to open your account in international cricket! A lovely delivery, it has been tossed up generously and lands a touch short around leg. Kane Williamson stands back inside the crease to defend it late but it spins away to beat the outside edge and goes on to clip the top of the off stump. Beauty from Usama and Mohammad Rizwan also flashes a smile. Completely bamboozled a batter of Kane's calibre. New Zealand will have to rebuild again.
Fuller and on off, it's eased down to long off for a single.
Close to off, on a length and angling in, Kane defends it back fro the crease.
A hint of swing in the air. Full and around off, Williamson strokes it down to mid on.
Fuller in length and wide outside off, Williamson plays a sublime drive to the right of sweeper cover. Gets a couple.

FOUR! Edgy! Short in length and around off, Kane Williamson goes on the back foot to force it through covers but it takes the inside edge and races past the stumps. Haris Rauf puts in a dive near the fence but fails to keep it in. He seems to have hurt himself in the process and is limping around.
Fuller this time, around off at 140.4 kph, Kane drives but finds the fielder at short cover.
Lands it on a length and around off, at 139 kph, Kane stays back and taps it down to short third man.
Floated and full, around off, Mitchell leans forward and pushes it with an angled bat to short third man.
FOUR! Put away! Usama Mir bowls it quicker and flatter through the air, it's short and on middle, Daryl Mitchell goes on the back foot and heaves it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Drags his length short and delivers it around off, Daryl Mitchell goes on the back foot and steers it to deep point for a couple.
Loopy and on middle, Mitchell is forward as he blocks it back.
Shortish and on off, defended back to the bowler.
Flighted and full, around off, Williamson drives it through covers for a single.
Full and on off, at 141 kph, Daryl Mitchell uses the angle and flicks but finds the mid-wicket fielder. He misfields but no run is taken.
Fuller in length and outside off, 139.3 kph, Kane drives it on the up and finds the gap at covers. Calls for two but gets only a run.
A touch short and around off, again Kane plays from the back foot and forces it to the off side. The cover fielder makes the stop to his left.
On a length and outside off at 140.3 kph, Kane pushes it from the back foot to cover-point.
Fuller and on off, at 139.3 kph, Mitchell pushes it gently to mid on and picks up a quick run.
Serves it on a length and close to off, at 140.4 kph, Williamson guides it down to third man for a single.
Bowls it short again, around off, Williamson goes back and forces it to sweeper cover for one. A decent over from Mir, looked nervous and bowled quite a few half-trackers.
Tossed up around off, fuller in length, Williamson defends it off the front foot.
Another short ball outside off, Mitchell slaps it through covers for another run.
Short in length and wide outside off, Williamson cuts it from the back foot to sweeper cover. Takes a single. 50 up!
Flighted delivery, full and around off, Daryl Mitchell gets forward and softly drops it towards cover-point for a brisk single.
Starts with a short delivery, outside off and spinning away, Daryl leaves.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over. Also, debutant Usama Mir comes into the attack.

Back of a length outside off by Mohammad Wasim, Kane Williamson tries to steer this one fine on the off side but fails to get it past backward point. At the end of Powerplay 1, New Zealand have scored 48 runs for the loss of two wickets.
Full and outside off, Kane Williamson blocks this one out down the wicket.

FOUR! Beautifully played! Mohammad Wasim bowls this one shorter and outside off, Kane Williamson lets the ball come to him and punches this one off the back foot. Gets it past cover and collects a boundary.
Back of a length around off, Daryl Mitchell taps this one gently towards mid on and takes a quick single.
On a length and outside off by Mohammad Wasim, Daryl Mitchell takes a step forward and defends this one back to the bowler.
Short of a length outside off, Daryl Mitchell uses his feet and defends this one to covers for a dot.

FOUR! Haris Rauf misses his line and pays the price! Bowls it short and wide outside off, Kane Williamson has all the time in the world to rock back and cut this one along the ground. Gets it past backward point for a boundary.
Tad fuller outside off, Kane Williamson drives this one on the up but away from the body. Fails to thread the gap in the cover region.
Good running! Haris Rauf bowls this one on a length at the stumps, Daryl Mitchell stays in the crease and taps it towards mid on and rushes for a quick single.
Sharp delivery. On a length around middle, at 143 clicks, skidding off the surface, Mitchell tries to work across the line but gets a soft leading edge. The ball rolls to cover-point.
Again the length is on the shorter side, at 145.1 kph, Daryl Mitchell defends it from the back foot to cover-point.
Back of a length and outside off, at 140.5 kph, Mitchell defends it down on the surface, from the back foot.
Change of ends for Haris Rauf.
Touch fuller and angling in at the stumps, Kane Williamson clips this one straight to mid-wicket for a dot.
Back of a length outside off, Kane Williamson opens the bat-face to steer this one fine on the off side but fails to get it past gully.
Short in length and outside off, Mitchell stands back and forces it through backward point for a single.
Daryl Mitchell is in next, at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mohammad Wasim strikes in his first over and removes Finn Allen! Mohammad Wasim bangs this one short and outside off at 141.2 kph, Finn Allen tries to muscle this one through the off side but does not get the proper connection on it. Mishits this one uppishly towards Agha Salman who takes a good catch diving to his right. Pakistan will be relieved to see the back of Finn Allen.
Commentary.Howout: c Agha Salman b Mohammad Wasim

Commentary.Commentary: Short and outside off by Mohammad Wasim, Kane Williamson lets the ball come to him and whips this one off the back foot to the right of mid on for a single.
Mohammad Wasim starts with a back-of-a-length delivery outside off, the ball keeps a bit low and Kane Williamson pushes this one to point for a dot.
Mohammad Wasim comes into the attack, replacing Haris Rauf.
Another heavy ball, on a length around off at 142.8 clicks, Finn stays on the back foot and defends it down.
Excellent running between the wickets. A length ball on middle, at 143.6 kph, Williamson bunts it to mid on for a quick run.

Naseem Shah bowls this one back of a length on off, Kane Williamson tries to defend this one but gets it from the outer part of the bat. It goes past backward point and Kane Williamson comes back for the second run.
Fuller outside off, Kane Williamson blocks this one out from the crease for a dot.

On a length around off, Finn Allen pushes this one towards mid off and sets off for a quick single. Babar Azam there collects it but decides to throw at the striker's end. Finn Allen would have been in trouble had Babar Azam hit at the non-striker's end.

FOUR! Finn Allen is in no mood to stop here! Banged in short and on middle by Naseem Shah, Finn Allen picks the length early and pulls this one to the left of the deep square leg fielder for a boundary.
Haris Rauf persists with short stuff, bowls this one around off and Kane Williamson pushes it off the back foot towards mid off for a dot.
Short and outside off, Kane Williamson stays in the crease and punches this one straight to point for a dot.
LEG BYE! Back of a length and angling in, Finn Allen tries to clip this one off his hips but fails to get any bat on it. The ball comes off his pads and rolls towards fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Haris Rauf goes back to short length, bowls this one at the batter, Finn Allen stands tall and uses the pace of the delivery to pull this one towards deep backward square leg for a boundary.
FOUR! TWO IN TWO! Fuller and angling onto the pads by Haris Rauf, Finn Allen lets the ball come to him and rolls his wrists to clip this one past mid-wicket for another boundary.
FOUR! Short and punished! Haris Rauf bowls this one back of a length outside off, Finn Allen shuffles across and punches this one along the ground. Gets it past extra cover and collects a boundary.
Short in length and outside off, Williamson plays his trademark dab but Pakistan have plugged that area. It's stopped at short third man. Dot ball to end the over, 9 runs off it.
Lands it on a length, around off at 143.5 kph, Finn pushes it off the inner half to mid on and pinches a single.
FOUR! Stand and delivery, Allen has had enough. Full in length and outside off, at 116.7 kph, Allen picks up the slower one early and smacks it over the bowler's head for a boundary, at long on.
Width there outside off, short in length, Allen slaps it to cover-point where Mohammad Nawaz makes a diving stop.
FOUR! Here comes the first boundary of the ODI series. Fuller in length and around off at 144.7 kph, Allen drills his drive through the line and finds the gap at extra cover for a boundary.
Short and wide outside off, Allen mistimes his shot towards the cover fielder.
Back of a length, around off at 144 clicks, Williamson times his shot from the back foot but picks up the cover fielder.
Fractionally short and outside off, at 142.4 kph, Williamson taps it down to the right of point. Imam makes a tumbling stop and Kane shouts a loud 'no' for a run.
Sliding down the leg side, at 143.3 kph, Williamson quietly deflects it off his pads to deep backward square leg. Takes two runs.
Full in length and around off, at 141.8 clicks, Kane gets forward and gently pushes it with an angled bat to backward point.
A 142.2 kph shortish ball on off, Allen punches again and this time back past the bowler. The mid on fielder mops it up and they rotate the strike.
Back of a length around off, at 144.5 kph, Allen is on his toes as he punches it back towards the bowler.
Fuller and on off, Williamson presses forward and drives it back to the bowler, off the inner half.
Pitches it up and outside off, at 143.4 kph, Williamson drives off the front foot but finds the fielder at point.
Around off, full and angling in at 141.2 kph, Williamson defends it off his front foot to short cover.
Length delivery around off, at 142.3 kph, Allen drives it to the left of the cover fielder. He stops it with a dive and they cross. Aleem Dar gestures for Allen to stay away from the danger area.

Risky single and a direct hit would have been close at the bowler's end. Fuller in length, around off at 137.8 kph, Williamson drives it to mid off and sets off for a quick run. Babar has a shy but misses. Would have been out, tells the replay.
Beaten! A lazy attempt from Kane. On a length and wide outside off, at 143.2 kph, Williamson uncharacteristically chases it away from his body and misses.
Lands it on a length outside off, Allen is on the back foot as he defends it from the inner portion of his bat. A tidy over, maiden!
Edgy! There is a lack of bounce on this 146 kph delivery, full and around off, Allen pushes at it and gets a bottom edge. It goes rolling to the keeper.

Given lbw! Finn Allen has a long chat with his skipper and takes the DRS at the very last moment. Haris Rauf dishes out a length ball around off and gets it to angle in at 143.3 kph, Finn Allen hangs back inside the crease, in his attempt to flick it across the line but misses. They appeal and the finger goes up after a while. DRS time! Nothing on the UltraEdge and the Ball Tracking shows that it's missing the stumps. Finn survives!
Puts it on a length and close to off, at 144.3 kph, Allen tries to drive but it takes the inner edge and goes to square leg. Three dots.
Fuller in length and on middle, at 143.7 kph, Allen tries to flick but fails to close the face of his bat in time. It takes the leading half of his blade and rolls tamely to mid on.
Lands it on a good length around off, Allen stays on the back foot and defends it down solidly.
Kane Williamson walks in at number 3 for New Zealand. Also, it will be Haris Rauf to operate with the second new ball from the other end.

OUT! BOWLED! Early success for Pakistan as Conway is dismissed for a golden duck. Shah delivers it fast and full, around leg, Devon Conway tries to work it on the leg side but misses. It clips the toe of his back leg, unluckily, and gets deflected onto the stumps. Naseem Shah is running in excitement and New Zealand suffer an early setback. Conway has been a consistent performer for them and this is a rare failure for him.
New Zealand are underway! The line is a bit straighter, on a shortish length at 141.5 kph, Allen turns it towards square leg where the fielder makes a diving stop. The batters cross.
Keeps it close to off and on a fuller length, at 140.2 kph, Allen gets behind the line and pushes it back towards Naseem.
Delivers it full and on off, at 141.8 kph, Allen gets on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler. We have not seen much movement so far.
Make it another leave. Full and outside off, Finn has a close look at the line and then offers no shot. For how long can he resist?
Shah begins with a length delivery, in the channel outside off, Finn Allen wants a sighter and leaves it alone.

Right then, we are done with the national anthems and we are all set for the action to start. The umpires and players make their way out in the middle. Finn Allen and Devon Conway will be the openers for New Zealand. Naseem Shah will start the proceedings with the first new ball for Pakistan. One slip in place. Here we go...
We are moments away from the first ball in this first ODI but before that, it's time for the national anthems. It will be New Zealand's first followed by Pakistan's.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Finn Allen, Kane Williamson (C), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (WK), Glenn Phillips, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Henry Shipley (On debut), Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Imam-ul-Haq, Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Haris Sohail, Agha Salman, Mohammad Nawaz, Usama Mir (On debut), Mohammad Wasim, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf.
TOSS - The coin toss lands in the favour of Pakistan and they have opted to bowl first.

We have some news coming in from the Pakistan camp - Usama Mir is all set to make his ODI debut today. The leg-spinner was one of the top performers in the recently concluded Pakistan Cup 2022-23 as he took 28 wickets from 11 matches.

New Zealand had a torrid end to their ODI season away from home, losing 3-0 in Australia, and they will look to put that series loss behind them and start afresh in 2023. The Kiwis will play this series under the leadership of their white-ball skipper, Kane Williamson. The visitors will be without the services of Trent Boult and Matt Henry, but they have good depth in the pace attack to make up for their absence. Having finished runners-up at the 2019 ODI World Cup, New Zealand will look to put their best foot forward in the lead-up to 2023’s 50-over event. Will the visitors draw first blood in the series, or will we see the hosts take the lead? We shall find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly.

Pakistan had a great ODI season at home in 2022, winning a series against Australia and West Indies and they will be keen to start the new year where they left off. The hosts will continue to be led by Babar Azam, and the skipper has some new faces at his disposal. Although Shadab Khan and Shaheen Afridi are missing out due to injuries, it is time for others to step up and claim a spot in the Pakistan side for the 2023 ODI World Cup.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the 1st ODI between Pakistan and New Zealand at the National Stadium in Karachi. With the ODI World Cup scheduled to be played later in the year, both teams will be eager to kickstart their preparations for that event on a winning note.
... MATCH DAY …

After a closely fought two-match Test series that ended in a draw and both sides sharing the trophy, it is now time for some white-ball action. Pakistan and New Zealand now battle it out in a three-match ODI series with all three ODIs to be played at the National Stadium in Karachi. Pakistan continue to be without the services of the spearhead of their attack, Shaheen Afridi. Moreover, the hosts were dealt a major blow in their preparations for the ODI series as leg spinner Shadab Khan was ruled out of the series with a finger injury. However, their pace bowling will be boosted by the return of Haris Rauf who missed the Test series due to a quad injury. Pakistan also have Mohammad Hasnain, Mohammad Wasim and Naseem Shah in the pace department. The spin-bowling duties for the hosts rest on the shoulders of Mohammad Nawaz and the uncapped trio of Tayyab Tahir, Kamran Ghulam and Usama Mir. In the batting department, Pakistan will be dependent on their captain Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood and Imam-ul-Haq. New Zealand will be led by Kane Williamson who returns to lead them in ODIs. The visitors have Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson, Matt Henry and Blair Tickner in their ranks as seaming options. In the spinning department, they will rely on Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi and Michael Bracewell. The onus will also be on Tom Latham, Finn Allen and Devon Conway to contribute with the bat and help the visitors put up a good show in this series. Who will draw first blood and take a 1-0 lead in the series? We shall find out together.
